title: Regional covariance added to Antarctic winter sea-ice variance in 2016-2025
abstract: We tested whether five Antarctic regions had more aligned winter sea-ice fluctuations in 2016-2025 than in 1989-2015. We used June-August mean extent from Sea Ice Index Version 4 and removed each period mean. The variance ratio rose from 0.669 to 1.736. The change in cross-region covariance accounts for 78.1% of the increase in total sample variance. The 95% interval for the ratio change is [0.068, 1.783] with two-year blocks, but [-0.084, 1.723] with three-year blocks. The recent ratio remains above 1 after removal of 2023 or linear trends. The result shows a sample shift from opposing to adding regional fluctuations. Ten recent winters cannot establish a lasting regime or a physical cause.

display.caption: Winter regional extent, centered correlations, and variance ratios. The recent interval uses two-year blocks. Credit: Sea Ice Index, National Snow and Ice Data Center.
